2  JUDGMENT Petitioner is a public limited company engaged in the activity of growing and manufacture of tea at its various factories including one at Pullivasal estate, following stringent safety measures to ensure,t tea is manufactured and packed in accordance with industrial standards.

Due to discrepancies in the testing methods for analysing tea samples, 1st respondent issued Ext.P3 order wherein, it is observed, it would not be appropriate to rely on test results for iron filings in tea and therefore, directed that, till such time the method of assessment is finalised, no testing should be done and factories should only be visited to ensure that necessary equipments are in place.

According to the petitioner, despite Ext.P3 binding order of the 1st respondent, and knowing that there are discrepancies in the testing method for tea which is likely to distort the test results, the 3rd respondent functioning under the 1st respondent arbitrarily and illegally proceeded to take samples from the petitioner's factory and have the same tested, resulting in Ext.P2 analysis report of the Food Analysit.

It is the contention of the petitioner that, it is with the intention of harassing the petitioner and initiating criminal proceedings, Ext.P2 is passed without taking into account Ext.P3 binding order passed by the 1st respondent.
It is in this background, seeking appropriate direction against Ext.P2 and for a direction to the respondents to adhere to Ext.P3 this writ petition is filed.

2. First respondent has filed a statement basically contending that 1st respondent has issued further instruction vide order dated 19.5.2016, whereby all concerned were directed that, until the method of assessment/testing of tea is finalised, the Enforcement Authorities may carry out inspections in tea factories rather than on retail outlets.
Therefore, according to the learned counsel for 1st respondent, 1st respondent is vested with power to visit the factory and secure samples.

It is also contended, as per regulation No.2.10.1 of Food Safety and Standards (Food Products and Food Additives) Regulations,2011, a standard is fixed, wherein presence of iron filings, is permitted upto 150 ppm, whereas Ext.P2 Analysis Report shows that the iron filings are more in quantity than the prescribed limit as per the Regulation.

sentences.text:
3. Heard learned counsel for the petitioner, learned counsel appearing for the 1st respondent and perused the documents on record and the pleadings put forth by the respective parties.
4.

The sole question to be considered is whether in view of Ext.P3 order passed by the 1st respondent, respondents are entitled as of right to enter the factory premises and secure samples in order to analyse the same ?
It can be seen that, the issue raised in this writ petition revolves round Ext.P3 .

Paragraph 3 of Ext.P3 reads thus:
"Until the method of assessment is finalised, the Enforcement Authorities may carry out inspections in Tea factories rather than on retail outlets, etc. to ensure that FBOs involved in the processing/manufacture of Tea operate with the requisite equipment for removal of iron filings."
5.

On a reading of Ext.P3, it is clear, the power conferred on the authorities is only to ensure that the FBOs involved in the processing /manufacture of tea operate with the requisite equipment for removal of iron filings.

Therefore, in my considered opinion, even if any sample is secured by the Tata Global Beverages Limited vs Food Safety And Standard Authority Of ... on 10 August, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/127215047/
3 respondents from the factory, the same cannot result in any penal or other consequences till such time the proceedings pursuant to Ext.P3 attain a logical conclusion.

sentences.text: Therefore, I am of the considered opinion that, even if Ext.P2 is drawn by the 1st respondent, the same will not have any consequence of any nature as provided under the Act till such time Ext.P3 attains a finality.

In that view of the matter, I hold that, respondents shall not initiate any action pursuant to Ext.P2 Analysis Report against the petitioner till such time a finality is attained as per Ext.P3 directives.
Writ petition is disposed of accordingly.
